### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. polycystic kidney disease 8  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.784)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:13387)

**Proposed mechanism:** NEK8 (HGNC:13387) —DISRUPTS→ ciliogenesis and planar cell polarity (GO:0007411); ciliogenesis and planar cell polarity (GO:0007411) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal kidney tubule morphology (HP:0000084); ciliogenesis and planar cell polarity (GO:0007411) —LEADS_TO→ Cystic kidney disease (HP:0000056). Loss-of-function mutations in NEK8 disrupt ciliogenesis and planar cell polarity pathways, leading to abnormal kidney tubule morphology and cystic kidney disease.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a common, high-frequency (MAF > 0.01) pathogenic variant in NEK8 in both disease populations that exhibits a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect. _(variant: HGNC:13387)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NEK8 in ciliogenesis provides a common therapeutic target for both MONDO:0013444 and polycystic kidney disease 8, potentially through modulators of this pathway.

#### 2. renal-hepatic-pancreatic dysplasia 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.715)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:13387)

**Proposed mechanism:** NEK8 (HGNC:13387) —DISRUPTS→ Nephronophthisis pathway (GO:0035565); Nephronophthisis pathway (GO:0035565) —DISRUPTS→ Ciliary function; Ciliary function —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal renal and hepatic development (HP:0001423); Ciliary function —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal pancreatic development (HP:0002070). Loss-of-function mutations in NEK8 disrupt the nephronophthisis pathway, leading to impaired ciliary function. This dysfunction in cilia affects multiple organs, manifesting as abnormal renal, hepatic, and pancreatic development, thereby linking the two diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in NEK8 that are clearly segregated with only one of the two diseases, or demonstration that NEK8 mutations primarily affect distinct downstream pathways for each disease. _(variant: Absence of common pathogenic variants in NEK8 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NEK8 in ciliopathies affecting renal, hepatic, and pancreatic development could lead to convergent therapeutic strategies targeting ciliary function or downstream effectors for patients with either condition.
